class.name: BulletFlock2D
class.brief_description: Flocking rules (boids) for bullets: separation, alignment, cohesion and their ranges.
class.description: One resource = one flock's rules. Assign it to [member BulletSpawner2D.flock] (with [member BulletSpawner2D.flock_enabled]) or join a volley with [method BulletVolley2D.flock_join], and the bullets fly as a boids flock: every physics tick each bullet looks at its flockmates and turns its heading toward a mix of three wishes, each weighted per second: - [member separation]: away from flockmates closer than [member separation_range], harder the closer they are; - [member alignment]: the mean flight heading of its flockmates within [member neighbor_range]; - [member cohesion]: the center of its flockmates within [member neighbor_range]. Only the direction turns: the speed stays the speed data's (acceleration, max speed and time scale keep working). The heading approaches the wished one by [code]1 - e^(-strength * delta)[/code] of the angle each tick, so it never overshoots and looks the same at any frame rate. WHO flies together is decided where the flock is armed ([member BulletSpawner2D.flock_scope], the scope of [method BulletVolley2D.flock_join]); separate flocks never see each other. Edits reach every bullet already in flight on the next tick ([code]swarm.cohesion = 2.0[/code]). Every accepted change emits [signal Resource.changed]; a rejected value pushes an error and keeps the old one. Homing turns first and the flock bends the result: give homing a turn rate ([member BulletVolleyData2D.homing_smoothing] above 0) so a homing swarm has room to flock. Direction curves in Override mode win their axis. Frozen bullets are not flockmates, and bullets of a frozen bullet world (time scale 0) do not turn. Cost: one pass per physics tick over every flocking bullet (an exact spatial hash grid), a few nanoseconds per flockmate looked at; [member max_neighbors] bounds the work per bullet and [member update_interval] spreads it over several ticks. Nothing is paid while no bullet flocks.

members.member: Per second: how hard each bullet turns toward the mean flight heading of its flockmates within [member neighbor_range]. 0 turns this rule off. Finite and >= 0.

Per second: how hard each bullet turns toward the center of its flockmates within [member neighbor_range] (stronger the farther the center is, relative to the range). 0 turns this rule off. Finite and >= 0.

When on, every flock turn also turns the bullet's rotation (sprite and collision shape) to face the new heading, so arrows and fish keep facing where they fly, even when homing snaps the heading toward its target every tick. Rotation data that spins the bullet owns the sprite and is left alone. When off, only the flight direction turns; a rotation that drives the heading ([member BulletVolleyData2D.adjust_direction_based_on_rotation], or homing that steers through the rotation) still follows it, or the flock's turn would be undone.

Flockmates each bullet reads per tick, nearest cells first (0 = no limit). Bounds the cost of dense swarms: a stack of N bullets costs exactly N x max_neighbors distance checks. The scan start rotates per bullet, so a capped flock has no drift bias. Real starlings track about 7.
Caps how fast the flock can turn a bullet, in degrees per second (0 = no cap). Keeps swarms fair to dodge. Homing and other steering are not capped by it.
Pixels: flockmates closer than this count for [member alignment] and [member cohesion] (the visual range). Finite and > 0.

Per second: how hard each bullet turns away from flockmates closer than [member separation_range], weighted by [code]1 - distance / separation_range[/code] so touching flockmates push hardest. Stacked bullets (same position) part along a fixed direction per pair. 0 turns this rule off. Finite and >= 0.
Pixels: flockmates closer than this push the bullet away (the protected range). Independent of [member neighbor_range] (it may be larger). 0 turns separation off.

Seconds of bullet time between two steering updates of a bullet (0 = every physics tick, the default). A positive interval recomputes each bullet once per interval, staggered across the flock so the work spreads evenly over the ticks; in between, every bullet keeps turning toward its last steering and still counts as a flockmate for the others. The flock pass costs roughly 1 / (interval x physics ticks per second) of the every-tick cost, so [code]3.0 / 60.0[/code] cuts it to a third with hardly a visible difference. A bullet with no steering yet (a new or reused volley, a bullet woken from a freeze) computes at once.

Field of view in degrees, centered on each bullet's flight heading: flockmates outside it are ignored by every rule (and do not count toward [member max_neighbors]). 360 (the default) sees all around; 180 sees only what is ahead, which turns a loose flock into leader-and-follower streams. Stacked flockmates (same position) are always seen so a stack still parts, and a bullet with no heading sees all around. Between 0 and 360.

constants.constant: The bullets of one spawner flock together. For [method BulletVolley2D.flock_join] on a factory volley: the factory's own volleys of this flock.
Every spawner and volley using this resource with this scope is ONE flock.
Each volley (one shot) is its own flock.
